name: OR-02
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Bentz running with a large cash advantage ($1.4M vs $54K)
No polls or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The seat's R+14 lean, Bentz's incumbency and roughly 15-to-1 fundraising edge over Chris Beck, and markets pricing him near 94% all point the same direction, with no polling or ratings evidence suggesting otherwise.
model.watch: A surprise scandal, retirement, or a major outside-spending influx for Beck would be the main ways this moves off Safe R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Eastern and southern Oregon's 2nd District is solidly Republican territory, and incumbent Cliff Bentz is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. He enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, holding about $1.4 million on hand to challenger Chris Beck's roughly $54,000, and no significant outside spending has materialized on either side.

Prediction markets give Bentz about a 94% chance of winning, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, Bentz's incumbency advantage, and the lopsided money race, all of which point to a comfortable Republican hold.
